bibl.title: Challenges of Sustainable and Commercial Aquaponics

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the published aquaponics literature, read for what would have to be known before a commercial system could be built - and found not to contain it
span.quote: However, there is a lack of quantitative research to support the development of economically feasible aquaponics systems. Although many studies have addressed some scientific aspects, there has been limited focus on commercial implementation.

span.label: what stands between aquaponics research and a commercially viable aquaponic farm, across technical, socio-ecological and economic dimensions
span.quote: The purpose of this paper is to highlight current aquaponics challenges and give directions for further research. For each challenge, various approaches are described.

span.label: a challenge inventory: for each obstacle the review names what is known, what is missing, and what would have to be measured - the missing half being the larger one
span.quote: The analysis shows that aquaponics is capable of being an important driver for the development of integrated food production systems. Arid regions suffering from water stress will particularly benefit from this technology being operated in a commercial environment.

span.label: critique
span.quote: The current literature cannot be used to critically assess and predict economic challenges; as presented in Table 2, only two economic sub-studies are available in the peer-reviewed literature

span.label: aquaponics - a closed loop in which fish waste feeds plants and the plants clean the water, so that the ecological weakness of each half becomes the other's input
span.quote: The system results in a symbiosis between fish, microorganisms and plants, and encourages sustainable use of water and nutrients, including their recycling ( Figure 1). Within this synergistic interaction, the respective ecological weaknesses of aquaculture and hydroponics are converted into strengths.

span.label: narrative review of the aquaponic literature with two comparison tables built from the published systems, one of design parameters and one of nutrient concentrations
span.term: narrative review of the aquaponic literature with two comparison tables built from the published systems, one of design parameters and one of nutrient concentrations
span.quote: With respect to Table 2, it is particularly noticeable that DWC systems are mainly used, and important design parameters such as fish to plant ratio or daily feed input are sometimes missing from the literature.

span.label: the two-step bacterial conversion the whole system rests on: nitroso-bacteria take ammonia to nitrite, nitro-bacteria take nitrite to nitrate, and the nitrate is both far less toxic to the fish and the plants' main nitrogen source
span.quote: The ammonia within the system is converted into nitrite (NO2−) by nitroso-bacteria, before being transformed into nitrate (NO3−) by the nitro-bacteria

span.label: two opposing forces act on system pH and one of them wins: nitrate uptake by roots RAISES pH by releasing bicarbonate, nitrification LOWERS it by producing acid, and the acid side has the larger effect, so the system drifts down continuously
span.quote: Although root uptake of nitrate raises pH as bicarbonate ions are released in exchange \ [49\], the acidity producing nitrification process has a higher impact on the overall system pH, leading to a constant and slight decrease in the pH-value.

span.label: the proposed fix for the drift - dissolved limestone releases hydroxide as it solubilizes, raising pH continuously at a rate set by the flow rate rather than in steps like a dosed buffer
span.quote: This water neutralization concept consists of the controlled addition of dissolved limestone (CaCO3) to the acid water that leads to a continuous pH-elevating effect due to carbonate solubilization that releases hydroxide anions (OH−).

span.label: why the nutrients may be present and unmeasured: in aquaponic water the dissolved solids include organic molecules, and the standard measurements register only the ionic fraction
span.quote: In hydroponics, TDS consists mainly of mineral compounds, while in aquaponics it includes organic molecules wherein nutrients can be locked up and overlooked by measuring procedures such as electrical conductivity (EC) or aqueous sample filtration. Both aqueous sample filtration and the EC measurement methods only take nutrients that are available in ionic form into account.

span.label: between 30% and 65% of the phosphorus entering as fish feed leaves as solid excretion and is filtered out, and what does dissolve can precipitate with calcium - which is why aquaponic phosphate sits far below the hydroponic recommendation
span.quote: In RAS, 30%–65% of the phosphorus added to the system via fish feed is lost in the form of fish solid excretion that is filtered out by either settling tanks or mechanical filters

span.label: the constraint that makes pest management hard: the system's function depends on a living nitrifying biofilm, so pesticides, antibiotics and fungicides are ruled out not by regulation but because they would kill the machinery
span.quote: Conventional pesticides that are used in hydroponics cannot be used in aquaponics because of toxicity risk to the fish and to the desired biofilm (e.g., autotrophic nitrifying biofilm)

span.label: only two economic sub-studies exist in the peer-reviewed literature, so the review states plainly that the literature cannot be used to assess economic viability at all
span.quote: The current literature cannot be used to critically assess and predict economic challenges; as presented in Table 2, only two economic sub-studies are available in the peer-reviewed literature

span.label: and the one integrated comparison it does find has nothing to be compared against
span.quote: Unfortunately, there are no other studies available for comparison.

span.label: the design table is built from published systems that often omit the parameters that matter most - fish-to-plant ratio, daily feed input
span.quote: With respect to Table 2, it is particularly noticeable that DWC systems are mainly used, and important design parameters such as fish to plant ratio or daily feed input are sometimes missing from the literature.

span.label: labour costs are excluded from the costings the review reproduces, so the financial picture is partial and the authors say so
span.quote: It must be mentioned that some costs (i.e., labor costs) are not taken into account, so the financial viability can only be partially estimated.

span.label: outside the UVI system there is little large-scale or long-duration literature, and much of what exists is a small-scale replicate of that one design - so the evidence base is narrower than its paper count suggests
span.quote: Apart from the UVI system, there is a lack of scientific literature when it comes to aquaponic experiments on large scale and during long time sequences. Moreover, many experimental setups published are small-scale replicates of the UVI design.

span.label: larger commercial systems do exist and their findings are confidential
span.quote: Experiments covering bigger production systems exist, but they are performed by private research centers or companies, whereby confidential findings are not always made accessible to third parties.

span.label: the microorganisms and the chemical and physical mechanisms of solubilization - the step the whole nutrient argument depends on - are not well understood
span.quote: All involved microorganisms and chemical and physical mechanisms of solubilization are not well understood

span.label: optimal nutrient levels for leafy and fruity vegetables in aquaponics are not established, so there is no target to engineer towards
span.quote: The optimal nutrient levels for leafy and fruity vegetables in aquaponics systems are not yet well established.

span.label: the health risk from the broad microflora aquaponics deliberately maintains has not been established either
span.quote: Since the presence of a broad range microflora belongs to aquaponic practices, the occurrence of pathogens and risk for human health should also be established, in order to assess the safety of aquaponics and to conduct appropriate quality control.

span.label: no general optimum exists - the system must be fitted to local climate, geography and market, which is the review's own limit on how far any of its recommendations travel
span.quote: Consequently, there is no general optimal system, as the system must be adjusted to environmental conditions.

span.label: printing Rakocy and Lennard's objection - that hydroponic and aquaponic nutrient solutions are not comparable - directly beside the table that compares them
span.note: eliminates: a reader taking the gap between the two columns as a real nutrient deficit, when part of it is an artefact of measuring only the ionic fraction of a solution that carries nutrients in organic form · outcome: held
span.quote: However, Rakocy and Lennard (pers. comm.) report that hydroponics and aquaponics nutrient solutions are not comparable for many reasons. The nature of the total dissolved solid (TDS) is not the same in these systems.

span.label: reporting that some aquaponic systems match or beat hydroponic yields DESPITE the lower measured mineral concentrations
span.note: eliminates: the lower concentrations being read as lower performance - the yields are the outcome and they do not follow the concentration table · outcome: held
span.quote: Hence, some aquaponics investigators report similar or even better yield than hydroponics for some crops, despite lower concentrations of mineral nutrients

span.label: naming which design parameters the published systems fail to report - fish-to-plant ratio, daily feed input - rather than presenting the comparison table as complete
span.note: eliminates: the table being read as a survey of how these systems were built, when for several of them the two parameters that determine the design are simply absent from the source · outcome: held
span.quote: With respect to Table 2, it is particularly noticeable that DWC systems are mainly used, and important design parameters such as fish to plant ratio or daily feed input are sometimes missing from the literature.

span.label: stating that the reproduced costings exclude labour
span.note: eliminates: the break-even and profit figures being read as complete - the review says explicitly that viability can therefore only be partially estimated · outcome: held
span.quote: It must be mentioned that some costs (i.e., labor costs) are not taken into account, so the financial viability can only be partially estimated.

span.label: attaching a caution to Rakocy's finding that basil out-earns lettuce by nearly four times
span.note: eliminates: a single system's crop-choice result being generalised, when the margin depends on a particular domestic market · outcome: held
span.quote: In an initial economic analysis, given the University of Virgin Islands (UVI) system design, they had a profit margin with basil exceeding almost by a factor 4 of that of lettuce. This finding should be viewed with a degree of caution because of different domestic market dependencies.

span.label: naming one specific unreported variable in a study it otherwise relies on - light intensity, absent from Rakocy et al.
span.note: eliminates: the two systems in the table being treated as comparable on plant yield, when a major determinant of that yield is unrecorded for one of them · outcome: held
span.quote: For example, light intensity (lm) was not reported by Rakocy et al. \ [24\], yet this is one of the major factors affecting plant growth and thus the harvested biomass.

span.label: aquaponics
span.quote: Aquaponics combines hydroponics and recirculating aquaculture elements. Conventional hydroponics requires mineral fertilizers in order to supply the plants with necessary nutrients but the aquaponics systems use the available fish water that is rich in fish waste as nutrients for plant growth.

span.label: hydroponics
span.quote: Aquaponics combines hydroponics and recirculating aquaculture elements. Conventional hydroponics requires mineral fertilizers in order to supply the plants with necessary nutrients but the aquaponics systems use the available fish water that is rich in fish waste as nutrients for plant growth.

span.label: recirculating aquaculture
span.quote: Aquaponics is an integrated multi-trophic system that combines elements of recirculating aquaculture and hydroponics \ [1\], wherein the water from the fish tanks that is enriched in nutrients is used for plant growth.

span.quote: The ammonia within the system is converted into nitrite (NO2−) by nitroso-bacteria, before being transformed into nitrate (NO3−) by the nitro-bacteria

span.label: nitro-bacteria
span.quote: The ammonia within the system is converted into nitrite (NO2−) by nitroso-bacteria, before being transformed into nitrate (NO3−) by the nitro-bacteria

span.quote: Although root uptake of nitrate raises pH as bicarbonate ions are released in exchange \ [49\], the acidity producing nitrification process has a higher impact on the overall system pH, leading to a constant and slight decrease in the pH-value.

span.label: nitrification
span.quote: Although root uptake of nitrate raises pH as bicarbonate ions are released in exchange \ [49\], the acidity producing nitrification process has a higher impact on the overall system pH, leading to a constant and slight decrease in the pH-value.

span.label: phosphorus
span.quote: In RAS, 30%–65% of the phosphorus added to the system via fish feed is lost in the form of fish solid excretion that is filtered out by either settling tanks or mechanical filters

span.label: electrical conductivity
span.quote: In hydroponics, TDS consists mainly of mineral compounds, while in aquaponics it includes organic molecules wherein nutrients can be locked up and overlooked by measuring procedures such as electrical conductivity (EC) or aqueous sample filtration. Both aqueous sample filtration and the EC measurement methods only take nutrients that are available in ionic form into account.

span.label: organic molecules
span.quote: In hydroponics, TDS consists mainly of mineral compounds, while in aquaponics it includes organic molecules wherein nutrients can be locked up and overlooked by measuring procedures such as electrical conductivity (EC) or aqueous sample filtration. Both aqueous sample filtration and the EC measurement methods only take nutrients that are available in ionic form into account.

span.label: biofilm
span.quote: Conventional pesticides that are used in hydroponics cannot be used in aquaponics because of toxicity risk to the fish and to the desired biofilm (e.g., autotrophic nitrifying biofilm)

span.label: pesticides
span.quote: Conventional pesticides that are used in hydroponics cannot be used in aquaponics because of toxicity risk to the fish and to the desired biofilm (e.g., autotrophic nitrifying biofilm)

span.label: sustainable agriculture
span.quote: Aquaponics can be considered a sustainable agricultural production system regarding the definition of Lehman et al. \ [10\], who define sustainable agriculture as a process that does not deplete any non-renewable resources that are essential to agriculture in order to sustain the agricultural practices.

span.label: water
span.quote: Compared to conventional agriculture, aquaponics uses less than 10% of water, depending on the climatic conditions

span.label: supply chain
span.quote: The longer the supply chain, the more transport, packaging, conservation and labor needed, leading to substantial decreases of resources and energy (e.g., up to 79% of the retail price in US conventional food distribution

span.label: conventional agriculture
span.quote: Compared to conventional agriculture, aquaponics uses less than 10% of water, depending on the climatic conditions

span.label: multi-disciplinarity
span.quote: The biggest challenge in commercial aquaponics is its multi-disciplinarity, needing further expertise in economics, finance and marketing.

span.label: supply chain → environmental impact
span.note: LENGTH OF A CHAIN AS A COST MULTIPLIER. The longer the supply chain the more transport, packaging, conservation and labour it needs, up to 79% of retail price in US conventional distribution. `causes` is right and the ENDPOINT is not a concept in this record - what lengthens is a chain and what grows is a bundle of costs and impacts, and there is no node for the bundle
span.quote: The longer the supply chain, the more transport, packaging, conservation and labor needed, leading to substantial decreases of resources and energy (e.g., up to 79% of the retail price in US conventional food distribution

span.label: pesticides → biofilm
span.note: A PROHIBITION, NOT A MEASURED EFFECT. Conventional pesticides cannot be used in aquaponics because they would poison the fish and the nitrifying biofilm the system depends on. `causes ... reduces` overstates it - nobody applied them and measured a reduction; the relation is that one RULES OUT the other, and the vocabulary has no type for a constraint
span.quote: Conventional pesticides that are used in hydroponics cannot be used in aquaponics because of toxicity risk to the fish and to the desired biofilm (e.g., autotrophic nitrifying biofilm)

span.label: electrical conductivity → organic molecules
span.note: THE MEASUREMENT THAT MISSES ITS OBJECT. Electrical conductivity and aqueous filtration register only nutrients in ionic form, so nutrients locked inside organic molecules are present and unrecorded. This is the exact negation CLAUDE_B's quine1951 row names: all eight edge types assert a relation HOLDS, and `X is the measurement that FAILS to see Y` cannot be written. `operationalised-as` would state the opposite of the truth
span.quote: In hydroponics, TDS consists mainly of mineral compounds, while in aquaponics it includes organic molecules wherein nutrients can be locked up and overlooked by measuring procedures such as electrical conductivity (EC) or aqueous sample filtration. Both aqueous sample filtration and the EC measurement methods only take nutrients that are available in ionic form into account.

span.label: sustainable agriculture - NOT DEFINED BY THIS PAPER. It is taken whole from Lehman et al., as a process that depletes no non-renewable resource essential to agriculture, and extended with Francis et al.'s `designing systems that close nutrient cycles`. Aquaponics then qualifies BY CONSTRUCTION, because closing a nutrient cycle is what it is. The definition is borrowed and the conclusion follows from the borrowing
span.quote: Aquaponics can be considered a sustainable agricultural production system regarding the definition of Lehman et al. \ [10\], who define sustainable agriculture as a process that does not deplete any non-renewable resources that are essential to agriculture in order to sustain the agricultural practices.

span.label: nutrient concentration, when an aquaponic solution is compared with a hydroponic one - A MEASUREMENT, NOT A QUANTITY OF NUTRIENT. Electrical conductivity and aqueous filtration see only ions, and aquaponic dissolved solids include organic molecules with nutrients locked inside them. So the aquaponic column reads lower partly because the instrument cannot see what is there - and the authors print the comparison and this objection to it on the same page
span.quote: In hydroponics, TDS consists mainly of mineral compounds, while in aquaponics it includes organic molecules wherein nutrients can be locked up and overlooked by measuring procedures such as electrical conductivity (EC) or aqueous sample filtration. Both aqueous sample filtration and the EC measurement methods only take nutrients that are available in ionic form into account.

span.label: challenge, the paper's own organising word - IT COVERS TWO DIFFERENT THINGS AND THE review does not separate them. Some challenges are engineering problems with candidate solutions (pH drift, and a lime-bed reactor to fix it). Others are ABSENCES IN THE LITERATURE - two economic studies, no comparison available, parameters unreported. A reader counting `challenges` counts both kinds together
span.quote: The current literature cannot be used to critically assess and predict economic challenges; as presented in Table 2, only two economic sub-studies are available in the peer-reviewed literature

span.label: decoupled system - THE NAME FOR GIVING UP ON THE COMPROMISE. Fish, plants and nitrifying bacteria have different optimal pH and temperature, and a single loop must sit between them; a decoupled system runs two loops at their own optima and exchanges water periodically. It is presented as an alternative to the trade-off, not as an improvement to it
span.quote: the physical separation in two recirculating loops, i.e., an aquaculture and hydroponic loop, described as decoupled systems, where optimal condition for each system is applied with periodic water exchange between them.

span.label: zero-discharge recirculating system - AN OBJECTIVE, NOT A DESCRIPTION. The paper says it `should be achievable` on Neori et al.'s authority and immediately says more research is needed on the solubilization it depends on. Nothing in the review reports one running
span.quote: Given the objective of obtaining a low environmental footprint, a zero-discharge recirculating system concept should be achievable according to Neori et al. \ [52\], but more research needs to be carried out on fish waste solubilization with the objective to transform all added nutrients into plant biomass.

span.label: critiques → Vermeulen and Kamstra, who found only a marginal cost reduction from aquaponics against RAS and hydroponics run separately
span.note: the objection is specific and it is about SCOPE, not arithmetic: the costing left out resource scarcity, and rising energy and fertilizer prices are expected to move the margin. The review does not claim the calculation was wrong
span.quote: Vermeulen and Kamstra \ [22\] report only a marginal cost reduction for environmental benefits of nutrient reuse and energy efficiency when aquaponics is compared to RAS and hydroponics run separately. However, this study did not take socio-ecological factors into account, such as operating in a resource (e.g., phosphorous, water) limited world. Energy cost and fertilizer prices are constantly rising and governmental policies encourage reduction of emitted pollution (e.g., tax incentive schemes), so this cost margin benefit of aquaponics is expected to rise.

span.label: builds-on → Lehman et al.'s definition of sustainable agriculture as a process that depletes no non-renewable resource essential to agriculture
span.quote: Aquaponics can be considered a sustainable agricultural production system regarding the definition of Lehman et al. \ [10\], who define sustainable agriculture as a process that does not deplete any non-renewable resources that are essential to agriculture in order to sustain the agricultural practices.

span.label: builds-on → Francis et al.'s addition that sustainable production means designing systems that close nutrient cycles
span.quote: Francis et al. \ [11\] add that sustainable agricultural production can be achieved by resembling natural ecosystems and “designing systems that close nutrient cycles”, which is one of the main characteristics of aquaponics.

span.label: qualifies → Rakocy's finding that leafy greens are more profitable than fruity vegetables, and that basil's margin in the UVI system exceeded lettuce's by nearly four times
span.quote: In an initial economic analysis, given the University of Virgin Islands (UVI) system design, they had a profit margin with basil exceeding almost by a factor 4 of that of lettuce. This finding should be viewed with a degree of caution because of different domestic market dependencies.

span.label: qualifies → Neori et al.'s position that a zero-discharge recirculating system is achievable
span.note: accepted as an objective and immediately made conditional on solubilization research that has not been done
span.quote: Given the objective of obtaining a low environmental footprint, a zero-discharge recirculating system concept should be achievable according to Neori et al. \ [52\], but more research needs to be carried out on fish waste solubilization with the objective to transform all added nutrients into plant biomass.

span.label: hydroponics —part-of→ aquaponics
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: Aquaponics is an integrated multi-trophic system that combines elements of recirculating aquaculture and hydroponics \ [1\], wherein the water from the fish tanks that is enriched in nutrients is used for plant growth.

span.label: recirculating aquaculture —part-of→ aquaponics
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: Aquaponics is an integrated multi-trophic system that combines elements of recirculating aquaculture and hydroponics \ [1\], wherein the water from the fish tanks that is enriched in nutrients is used for plant growth.

span.label: aquaponics —distinct-from→ hydroponics
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95 — and the difference is the nutrient source: hydroponics needs mineral fertiliser, aquaponics uses the fish water. That is why they are also in a part-of relation - aquaponics contains a hydroponic component but is not one
span.quote: Aquaponics combines hydroponics and recirculating aquaculture elements. Conventional hydroponics requires mineral fertilizers in order to supply the plants with necessary nutrients but the aquaponics systems use the available fish water that is rich in fish waste as nutrients for plant growth.

span.label: nitrification —causes→ pH
span.note: direction on the measure: reduces · strength of the relation: 0.95 — the winning force - the system drifts acid continuously and must be corrected
span.quote: Although root uptake of nitrate raises pH as bicarbonate ions are released in exchange \ [49\], the acidity producing nitrification process has a higher impact on the overall system pH, leading to a constant and slight decrease in the pH-value.

span.label: nitrate —causes→ pH
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.9 — the losing force, in the SAME sentence as the edge above. A schema that could not sign a causal edge would record these two as identical rows
span.quote: Although root uptake of nitrate raises pH as bicarbonate ions are released in exchange \ [49\], the acidity producing nitrification process has a higher impact on the overall system pH, leading to a constant and slight decrease in the pH-value.

span.label: ammonia —causes→ nitrite
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.95
span.quote: The ammonia within the system is converted into nitrite (NO2−) by nitroso-bacteria, before being transformed into nitrate (NO3−) by the nitro-bacteria

span.label: nitrite —causes→ nitrate
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.95
span.quote: The ammonia within the system is converted into nitrite (NO2−) by nitroso-bacteria, before being transformed into nitrate (NO3−) by the nitro-bacteria

span.label: aquaponics —causes→ water
span.note: direction on the measure: reduces · strength of the relation: 0.85 — the comparison is against conventional agriculture and the paper attaches a condition to it - `depending on the climatic conditions`
span.quote: Compared to conventional agriculture, aquaponics uses less than 10% of water, depending on the climatic conditions

span.label: the literature cannot support an economic assessment of aquaponics: two economic sub-studies exist in the peer-reviewed literature and one of them has nothing to compare against
span.quote: The current literature cannot be used to critically assess and predict economic challenges; as presented in Table 2, only two economic sub-studies are available in the peer-reviewed literature

span.label: the evidence base is narrower than its paper count: outside UVI there is little large-scale or long-duration work, and much of the rest replicates that one design
span.quote: Apart from the UVI system, there is a lack of scientific literature when it comes to aquaponic experiments on large scale and during long time sequences. Moreover, many experimental setups published are small-scale replicates of the UVI design.

span.label: the larger commercial systems exist and their results are confidential
span.quote: Experiments covering bigger production systems exist, but they are performed by private research centers or companies, whereby confidential findings are not always made accessible to third parties.

span.label: aquaponic nutrient concentrations sit below hydroponic recommendations for every element where data exist - AND some aquaponic systems match or beat hydroponic yields anyway
span.quote: Hence, some aquaponics investigators report similar or even better yield than hydroponics for some crops, despite lower concentrations of mineral nutrients

span.label: the reason may be measurement: EC and filtration see only ionic nutrients, and aquaponic water carries them inside organic molecules too
span.quote: In hydroponics, TDS consists mainly of mineral compounds, while in aquaponics it includes organic molecules wherein nutrients can be locked up and overlooked by measuring procedures such as electrical conductivity (EC) or aqueous sample filtration. Both aqueous sample filtration and the EC measurement methods only take nutrients that are available in ionic form into account.

span.label: the biggest challenge named is not technical but organisational - aquaponics needs expertise from fields that universities teach in different schools
span.quote: The biggest challenge in commercial aquaponics is its multi-disciplinarity, needing further expertise in economics, finance and marketing.

span.label: single-loop aquaponics is a compromise nobody's optimum: fish, plants and nitrifying bacteria want different pH and different temperatures
span.quote: Despite this fact, temperatures for warm water species such as tilapia and nitrifying bacteria can be 25 °C–30 °C, whereas most plants rather prefer colder water temperatures (approx. 20 °C–25 °C). Thus far, aquaponics has been built on a trade-off between the needs of fish and plants, respectively.

span.label: there is no general optimal system - it must be fitted to local climate, geography and market
span.quote: Consequently, there is no general optimal system, as the system must be adjusted to environmental conditions.

span.label: aquaponics = an integrated multi-trophic system combining recirculating aquaculture and hydroponics, in which nutrient-enriched fish-tank water grows the plants
span.quote: Aquaponics is an integrated multi-trophic system that combines elements of recirculating aquaculture and hydroponics \ [1\], wherein the water from the fish tanks that is enriched in nutrients is used for plant growth.

span.label: sustainable agriculture, borrowed from Lehman et al. = a process that does not deplete any non-renewable resource essential to agriculture
span.quote: Aquaponics can be considered a sustainable agricultural production system regarding the definition of Lehman et al. \ [10\], who define sustainable agriculture as a process that does not deplete any non-renewable resources that are essential to agriculture in order to sustain the agricultural practices.

span.label: and extended by Francis et al. to designing systems that close nutrient cycles - which the review immediately notes is a main characteristic of aquaponics
span.quote: Francis et al. \ [11\] add that sustainable agricultural production can be achieved by resembling natural ecosystems and “designing systems that close nutrient cycles”, which is one of the main characteristics of aquaponics.

span.label: decoupled system = two separate recirculating loops, aquaculture and hydroponic, each at its own optimum, with periodic water exchange between them
span.quote: the physical separation in two recirculating loops, i.e., an aquaculture and hydroponic loop, described as decoupled systems, where optimal condition for each system is applied with periodic water exchange between them.

span.label: zero-discharge recirculating system = the objective of transforming every added nutrient into plant biomass, stated as achievable and not demonstrated
span.quote: Given the objective of obtaining a low environmental footprint, a zero-discharge recirculating system concept should be achievable according to Neori et al. \ [52\], but more research needs to be carried out on fish waste solubilization with the objective to transform all added nutrients into plant biomass.

span.label: aquaponics uses under 10% of the water of conventional agriculture, which itself takes about 70% of available freshwater and up to 90% in arid regions
span.quote: On average, global agriculture uses around 70% of the available freshwater resources. In arid climate zones such as the Middle East and North Africa, the agricultural water consumption can even be up to 90%

span.label: 1 kg of beef takes 5,000-20,000 L of water; the same weight of fish in semi-intensive or extensive aquaculture takes 2,500-375,000 L
span.quote: In this respect, 1 kg of beef meat requires between 5000 and 20,000 L of water \ [16\] and the same amount of fish bred in semi-intensive and extensive conventional aquaculture systems requires a range of 2500–375,000 L

span.label: recirculating aquaculture reuses 95%-99% of its water, down to below 100 L per kg of fish
span.quote: Recirculating aquaculture systems, on the other hand, have a high degree of water reuse (i.e., 95%–99%) \ [18\], with water usage down to below 100 L kg−1 of fish produced

span.label: 30%-65% of the phosphorus entering as fish feed is filtered out as solid excretion
span.quote: In RAS, 30%–65% of the phosphorus added to the system via fish feed is lost in the form of fish solid excretion that is filtered out by either settling tanks or mechanical filters

span.label: aquaponic systems report 1-17 mg/L phosphate-P against a hydroponic recommendation of 40-60
span.quote: Consequently, aquaponic experiments report a range of 1–17 mg L−1 PO4-P \ [24, 31, 32, 38, 70, 80\]. However, recommended concentrations in standard hydroponics are generally between 40 and 60 mg L−1 PO4-P

span.label: 80% of the world's oceans are fully exploited or worse; 100 million tonnes of fish a year give 2.5 billion people at least a fifth of their animal protein
span.quote: Eighty percent of the world’s oceans are fully- or over-exploited, depleted or in a state of collapse. One hundred million tons of fish are consumed worldwide each year, providing 2.5 billion people with at least 20% of their average per capita animal protein intake

span.label: distribution can reach 79% of the retail price in US conventional food supply
span.quote: The longer the supply chain, the more transport, packaging, conservation and labor needed, leading to substantial decreases of resources and energy (e.g., up to 79% of the retail price in US conventional food distribution

span.label: the system pH target is 6.8-7.0, chosen as the highest value that still prevents ammonia accumulation
span.quote: Based on these data, the highest possible pH value should be consistent with the prevention of ammonia accumulation in the system. Then, the ideal pH value for the system is between 6.8 and 7.0.
